source.citation: Wiebe, R., Gaddy, V. L. (1940). The solubility of carbon dioxide in water at various temperatures from 12 to 40 C and at pressures to 500 atmospheres. Critical phenomena. Journal of the American Chemical Society 62(4), 815-817.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF from the publisher, a scan whose text layer is an OCR): Table I, p. 815, read on the page rendered at 500 dpi
transcription.note: Every value read on the image agrees with the OCR of the text layer up to its punctuation; the OCR has the entry at 125 atm and 40 C garbled, which the image gives as 28.71. The solubility is the volume of gas, reduced to 0 C and 1 atm (S. T. P.), dissolved per gram of water. Converted with the molar volume of the ideal gas at 0 C and 1 atm, 22414 cm3/mol, it gives the mole fractions Spycher et al. (2003, Appendix A) tabulate for these data, 1.127 % at 31.04 C and 25 atm and 3.014 % at 500 atm.

notes: Temperature in degrees Celsius; pressure in atmospheres, the total pressure over the solution; solubility in cubic centimeters of carbon dioxide at 0 C and 1 atm (S. T. P.) per gram of water.

The table has no value at 12 C and 25 atm, at 25 C and 25, 125, 150, 200, 300 and 500 atm, nor wherever else it is left blank; at 10 C and above 50 atm, and at 12 C above 300 atm, the authors report the formation of a solid hydrate.
